Two identical cars P and Q are travelling along a straight road. Car Q is travelling at twice the
speed of car P. The brakes are applied to both cars, producing the same constant deceleration.
Which graph shows how the velocity v of each car varies with time t ?

hints: Look at the $v$-intercept at $t=0$: the starting velocity of Q must be twice the starting velocity of P.
Recall what constant deceleration means for the shape of a $v$-$t$ graph: the gradient equals acceleration, so constant acceleration gives a straight line.
Use $t = u/a$ for stopping from speed $u$ with deceleration $a$ to compare the time for Q to stop with the time for P to stop when $a$ is the same.
walkthrough: Identify the givens: at $t=0$, $u_Q = 2u_P$, and both cars have the same constant deceleration of magnitude $a$.
State the $v$-$t$ rule: gradient $= dv/dt =$ acceleration. Constant negative acceleration gives a straight line sloping down.
Same deceleration means the same gradient, so the P line and Q line must be parallel straight lines.
Initial values fix the intercepts: the Q line must start at twice the $v$-value of the P line on the $v$-axis.
Stopping time follows from $v = u - at$. Setting $v=0$ gives $t = u/a$. So $t_P = u_P/a$ and $t_Q = 2u_P/a = 2t_P$.
Only the graph with parallel straight lines, Q starting twice as high as P and reaching $t$-axis at twice the time, satisfies all conditions. This is option C.

A.explanation: The two straight lines are not parallel, so the gradients and therefore the decelerations are different, which contradicts the same constant deceleration.

B.explanation: Both lines are curved, so the gradient is changing and the deceleration is not constant.

C.explanation: Both lines are straight with the same negative gradient for the same constant deceleration, with Q starting at twice the $v$ of P and taking twice the time to reach $v=0$.

D.explanation: Both lines are curved, so the gradient is changing and the deceleration is not constant.
